text.p: Ventritex Inc on Thrusday said the U.S. Food and Drug Administration has authorized it to proceed with a notification and reprogramming procedure for the 5,605 model V-110 and electrically similar V-112 defibrillators which are currently implanted in patients.

In a statement, the company said the move is in response to the recent failure of an electrical component in two implanted Cadence model V-110 defibrillators, which resulted in the delivery of inappropriately rapid pacing pulses.
The company said the rapid pacing is believed to have been associated with the induction of lethal ventricular tachyarrhythmias.
Both devices were implanted for approximately two years and the company said there have been no other incidents in which inappropriately rapid pacing pulses were delivered by Ventritex products.

Ventritex's current production models -- Cadet V-115 and Contour V-145 -- are not affected. The company said the reprogramming takes only a few minutes, does not require surgery and prevents the delivery of inappropriately rapid pacing pulses, even in the event of a component failure.
